subject: Convertible promo credits -> commitment proposal (LaunchHub)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@launchhub.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Promo credit conversion idea — LaunchHub

Hi Olga,

Quick ask — we have $25k of promotional credits from the accelerator that are scheduled to expire in 60 days. Our finance team is asking whether Redwood would consider a one-time conversion: we convert those promo credits into a prepaid commitment (we'd sign a 6–9 month reserved capacity commitment) in exchange for an additional committed discount on top of the standard Dedicated rate.

High level:
- Promo credits: $25,000 currently unspent
- Proposed commitment: 6–9 months of reserved capacity (T-shirt sizing: medium pool)
- Ask: apply the $25k toward the first invoice(s) post-commit, and give us an extra 8–12% on the committed price (on top of the base commit discount)

We're willing to sign a short addendum that documents the conversion mechanics. Main constraints from our side: the credits must be applied to committed billing (not purely promotional services), and we'd like the ability to use them for burst capacity in the first 90 days if needed.

Attaching a quick PDF with our numbers (discount-proposal.pdf). Can you let me know whether this is something Redwood would entertain and what the guardrails would be?

Thanks —
Samir
Head of Ops, LaunchHub

Ben / Kimberly — forwarding LaunchHub's request. They want to convert $25k of accelerator promo credits into a reserved commitment in exchange for an extra discount and want those credits to be applied to committed invoices (and possibly to cover burst).

Ben — can you assess standard flexibility on promo->commit conversions and whether sales can offer a one-off committed discount in exchange?
Kimberly — flagging Finance/tax implications — is it feasible to treat promo credits as an advance that is applied to committed invoices? Any constraints around revenue recognition or refund exposure we should be concerned about?

I think a pragmatic path (if allowed) is an addendum: convertible-credit clause that specifies timelines, how much of the promo is applied to first invoice(s), and service boundaries for burst usage.

Goal: get back to Samir with a proposed structure by EOD Thursday so they can decide ahead of their board meeting next week.

Thanks,
Olga
Sr. Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-09T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Promo credit conversion idea — LaunchHub

Olga / Kimberly — quick take from GTM side. Policy today: accelerator promo credits are normally non-convertible and expire at the promo window. That said, for good pipeline and retention outcomes we've done bespoke arrangements where promo credits are effectively treated as a prepayment and rolled into committed billing under specific controls.

Proposed commercial framing for LaunchHub:
- Offer: Convert up to $25k promo credits into an "applied credit" that Redwood will apply to the customer's committed invoices.
- Commitment term: prefer 9 months to smooth unit economics, but 6 months acceptable with slightly tighter pricing.
- Extra discount: propose an 8% additional discount on top of the standard commit tier if they do 9 months; 6% for 6 months.
- Application: allow up to $20k to be applied to the first committed invoice (covers first month + burst), remainder applies over next 2 invoices.
- Guardrails: credits cannot be refunded or transferred; conversion requires a signed addendum and SOW; credits expire if the customer terminates early (no refunds).

I've attached a draft addendum that legal can iterate on (credit-addendum-draft.docx). Operationally we can enable burst usage for the first 60 days subject to quota and capacity availability.

If we want to be more competitive we can increase the extra discount by 1–2 points, but Finance will need to sign off on recognition and margin impact.

Happy to present this to Samir if you want me on the call.

- Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Promo credit conversion idea — LaunchHub

Ben / Olga — finance perspective: converting promo credits into applied committed credits is workable but there are accounting considerations we must document. Key points:

1) Recognition: If we accept promo credits as consideration for a commitment, we need to treat the converted amount as deferred revenue recognized as we deliver committed compute capacity. That implies updated invoicing and revenue mapping.
2) Refund exposure: Because promo credits were issued originally as a marketing incentive, final conversion must include a clause that the credits are non-refundable once applied.
3) Burst usage: Allowing credits to cover burst is fine, but we should cap burst consumption allowed under the applied-credit to a defined multiplier (e.g., 1.5x committed baseline) and only within the first 60 days.
4) Tax / gift accounting: we should confirm no local tax liabilities arise on the conversion; recommend we run the addendum past Tax Counsel for larger deals.

Operational suggestion: make this a short-term, limited exception with the following controls:
- Apply up to $20k to first invoice; remainder rolled across next 2 monthly invoices
- Term: prefer 9 months; if customer requests 6 months increase the commit dollar/minimum by ~10% to preserve margin
- Include customer acknowledgement that credits are non-refundable and non-transferable

I'll attach a brief note summarizing these points (finance-note.txt). If Legal approves the addendum language I can sign off from Finance.

-Kimberly
Head of Revenue Ops & Finance

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the numbers. We spoke internally and can offer a limited, documented exception that converts up to $25k of your accelerator promo credits into an applied credit against a reserved commitment. Summary of our proposed structure below — please confirm whether this matches what you're seeking and whether you prefer a 6- or 9-month term. After you confirm we will issue an addendum for signature and provide a DocuSign link.

Proposed structure (Redwood -> LaunchHub):
- Convert: up to $25,000 accelerator promo credits into an applied committed credit
- Commitment term: 9 months preferred (monthly billing); 6 months acceptable with slightly different pricing
- Commercials: additional 9% committed discount on top of the standard Dedicated commit rate if 9 months; 6.5% if 6 months
- Application: up to $20k of applied credit may be used on the first invoice (including burst capacity charges within the first 60 days). Remaining $5k will be applied evenly across invoice 2 and 3.
- Controls: credits non-refundable, non-transferable; conversion requires signed addendum and SOW; credits void if customer terminates early (no cash back).
- Timeline: offer valid until 2026-09-18; we will prepare an addendum and DocuSign link once you confirm term choice.

Link to the proposed DocuSign (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/link/launchhub-convertible-credit

If you want a slightly deeper discount we can explore adjusting the commit size or length, but we'd need Finance sign-off. Let me know preference on 6 vs 9 months and whether you want Ben or me on a quick call to walk through the addendum.

Best,
Olga
Sr. Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

Olga — appreciate the quick turn. We're aligned in principle and would like to take you up on the conversion, with one tweak: would Redwood consider a 6-month commitment (we have a product milestone in Q1 that makes longer commitments tricky right now) with the following adjustments:

- 6-month term instead of 9 months
- Keep the applied credit mechanics (apply up to $20k on invoice 1, remainder across invoice 2/3)
- Can credits be used for burst capacity beyond baseline for the first 90 days? Our ops team wants the cushion for launch spikes.

If the 6-month pricing you proposed (6.5% extra) is firm we can move forward; otherwise if there's a way to meet in the middle at ~7% that would help justify the shorter term for our CFO. I'll have our legal review the addendum once it's sent. Attaching a short ops note with burst scenarios (ops-questions.pdf).

Can we get final paper by next Thursday 2026-09-18? If yes we'll route for signature immediately.

Thanks —
Samir
Head of Ops, LaunchHub
